holidays.name: International Cat Day
holidays.description: A day for cat lovers worldwide to celebrate their feline overlords, share cat photos, and cuddle with whiskered friends. Social media is basically taken over by furballs on this day.
holidays.origin: Created in 2002 by the International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) to raise awareness about cats and to encourage people to care for them and for cats in need.
holidays.funFact: Cats sleep for roughly 12 to 16 hours a day, which means they spend about 70 percent of their lives napping. Truly an inspiring work-life balance.

holidays.name: Sneak Some Zucchini Onto Your Neighbor's Porch Night
holidays.description: A mischievous night when gardeners with way too much zucchini secretly leave bags of it on neighbors' porches, ring the doorbell, and run away like produce ninjas.
holidays.origin: An unofficial holiday born from gardeners' struggle with the zucchini plant's absurd productivity in late summer. It is traditionally celebrated on August 8 in the United States.
holidays.funFact: A single zucchini plant can produce up to 6 to 10 pounds of fruit in a season, and if left unpicked, a zucchini can grow to the size of a baseball bat in a matter of days.

holidays.name: Happiness Happens Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the simple idea that happiness just happens, with encouragement to notice small joys, do something nice for someone, and spread good cheer without needing a reason.
holidays.origin: Created by Valerie Wilson of Illinois, who wanted to remind people that happiness is available all the time and does not depend on special occasions.
holidays.funFact: Studies on gratitude suggest that simply writing down three good things each day can measurably boost mood for weeks, so Happiness Happens Day has some science on its side.

holidays.name: Dollar Store Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the glorious bargain bins of dollar stores, where you walk in for one item and walk out with a pool noodle, glitter glue, and seven novelty spatulas.
holidays.origin: An unofficial consumer holiday celebrating the discount retail phenomenon that has been a staple of American shopping since the first five-and-dime stores of the late 1800s.
holidays.funFact: The five-and-dime concept was pioneered by Frank Woolworth, who opened his famous 'Great Five Cent Store' in 1879, and his chain grew to be one of the largest retailers in the world.

holidays.name: Odie Day
holidays.description: A tribute to Odie, the lovable, drooling, goofy-looking beagle-ish dog from the comic strip Garfield, who is famously kicked off tables by a lasagna-loving orange cat.
holidays.origin: Observed as a fan-driven pop culture celebration in honor of the Garfield comic strip character created by Jim Davis, who first appeared in the strip in 1978.
holidays.funFact: Odie was originally introduced as a pet belonging to Garfield's roommate Lyman, and he became Jon Arbuckle's dog only after Lyman disappeared from the strip.
